coverageClaim: Recently verified studies covering selected priority taxa; not proof that no newer paper exists.

items.label: 2025 mitochondrial diversity
items.statement: A Greater Mindanao study found low mitochondrial nucleotide diversity among 32 Philippine Eagles.
items.source: Bacus et al. (2025), Ecology and Evolution 15:e72572
items.scopeLimit: 32 mitochondrial samples from the Greater Mindanao faunal region; not an estimate of population size or body morphology.

items.label: Maternal ancestry
items.statement: Mitochondrial analysis identified at least two maternal lineages in the 32 sampled eagles.
items.source: Bacus et al. (2025), Ecology and Evolution 15:e72572
items.scopeLimit: 32 mitochondrial samples from the Greater Mindanao faunal region; not an estimate of population size or body morphology.

items.label: 2025 reference genome
items.statement: The first published draft genome spans 2.52 billion base pairs and includes 24,531 annotated genes.
items.scopeLimit: First draft genome assembly; genomic resource, not a morphological field key.

items.label: 2026 nightly movement
items.statement: Two tagged golden-crowned flying foxes averaged 18.85 km of nightly linear movement in a Philippine tracking study.
items.scopeLimit: Tracking sample included only two Acerodon jubatus and covered at most 45 nights; not a species-wide movement standard.

items.label: Modified habitats
items.statement: Tracked flying foxes used built-up and agricultural habitats alongside other land-cover types.
items.scopeLimit: Tracking sample included only two Acerodon jubatus and covered at most 45 nights; not a species-wide movement standard.

items.label: Seagrass foraging trails
items.statement: A 2026 Singapore study measured 344 dugong feeding trails in seagrass meadows.
items.source: Ng et al. (2026), Global Ecology and Conservation 69:e04287
items.scopeLimit: 344 feeding trails measured in Singapore, outside the Philippines; no inference about local Philippine dugong populations.

items.label: Higher-biomass seagrass patches
items.statement: The Singapore study associated dugong feeding trails with higher-biomass patches in Halodule–Halophila meadows.
items.source: Ng et al. (2026), Global Ecology and Conservation 69:e04287
items.scopeLimit: 344 feeding trails measured in Singapore, outside the Philippines; no inference about local Philippine dugong populations.
